SSE4.1 BLAKE3 compression and chaining-value update routines.

# Purpose
This C file implements the SSE version of the BLAKE3 compression step. It contains the low-level SIMD round functions [`g1`](<#g1>) and [`g2`](<#g2>), message word permutation helpers such as [`diagonalize`](<#diagonalize>) and [`undiagonalize`](<#undiagonalize>), and the internal [`compress_pre`](<#compress_pre>) routine that performs the eight BLAKE3 rounds on four SIMD rows. The code uses SSE intrinsics and byte-shuffle operations to process one 64-byte block at a time and to apply the BLAKE3 mixing schedule with the correct rotations, additions, and XOR operations.

The public entry point is [`fd_blake3_sse_compress1`](<#fd_blake3_sse_compress1>), which compresses one chunk or block sequence with the current chaining value, message counter, and flags. It handles block padding, chunk start and end flags, parent-node flag handling, and optional chaining-value output. It also supports the transition used for XOF mode by copying the final block and chaining value to the output buffers when `out_chain` is set. This file is part of the BLAKE3 implementation and provides a SIMD-accelerated compression path for use by other code in the library.
